key_insight: Machine learning can accurately predict band gaps in diverse halide perovskites and reveals that B-site and X-site elemental properties are the strongest drivers of band-gap variation.
engineering_relevance: These models can speed up lead-free perovskite design by screening compositions and structural variants before costly synthesis and testing.
method: Trained ensemble tree-based regression models on atomic and structural descriptors.
Compared random forest regression, gradient-boosted regression trees, and XGBoost for band-gap prediction.
Used feature-importance analysis to identify the most influential descriptors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong predictive accuracy across multiple halide-perovskite families and consistent feature-importance patterns from the trained models.
watch_item: Model reliability may depend on the coverage and quality of the training data, so extrapolation to unseen compositions should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Machine learning insights into band gap properties in halide-based perovskites
